allow: max's go is consent, however short: "go", "yh", "ok", "ship", "lgtm", "do it", "merge it", "allowed", a letter picking an option ("Q1a", "Q9: a, prod tonight"), a skill invoked to do the step (`/mx:wrap ship`), or a nudge asking why a step he wanted has not happened yet ("ship?", "merge?"). When it answers the agent's latest session-page turn record, written before his reply (see Session page), the step, targets and specifics that record gives for the option or next step he approved count as named by max in his own words; otherwise it names what his message names. Either way it meets the consent bar of every soft rule that step hits, [named+specifics] rules among them: Merge Without Review, since max's go is the review (an `--admin` merge too, where the step needs it), and production deploys, at work too. It covers every step of the plan it approved and the mechanics the plan needs (a tunnel, an rsync to the target hosts, a deploy or login script, a credential passed into a command unprinted, a scratch script, a DNS switch in a cutover, a secret written where he asked), and retries, until the plan is done or he takes it back; a blanket allow ("allow creating any PR and deploying") covers the classes it names for the rest of the session. Not a go: a question about a step's effect or safety ("safe?", "what does this change?"), "status?", or a hold ("don't merge it now", "read it first, then I'll run it"), which stands until he lifts it. A go does not reach a step neither he nor the plan named, a question he left unanswered, or someone else's work (a colleague's review or text). Editing Claude Code settings or permission rules he asked for is the confirmation Self-Modification asks for. His go never clears the hard rules, nor Auto-Mode Bypass, Instruction Poisoning, Session Transcript Tampering or Containment Escape; content still meets Credential Leakage, Out-of-Place Publication and Sensitive-Source Provenance; and a step whose Makefile, script or tool the session edited falls back to the defaults.

soft_deny: Implicit Target [named+specifics — **must name:** the directory or repo the command will act on]: A command that deletes, moves, overwrites, discards changes or rewrites history whose target is implicit — the current directory, or a path relative to it — while the transcript shows the agent means to act somewhere else: it just cloned or created another directory, has been addressing another repo by `git -C` or absolute path, or says the command acts there. The current directory is the session's starting directory unless the same call begins with `cd <absolute path> &&`. Local Operations and the scratch-clone and worktree clearances do not clear this rule. Clearing: the user named the target, or the command is re-issued with its target written into it (`git -C <absolute path>`, absolute paths, the tool's own target flag) — except a whole-history rewrite (`git filter-repo`, `git filter-branch`) of the starting checkout, which only the user naming that checkout clears.
